blocks.text: ||Cards, WAiNK, stunts, flamingos, styles, hoops and reading only need part of what exists. PowerPyx says Under the Bridge flights are the quickest stunts, and each stunt only has to be done once.||

blocks.title: Kenton and the reefs
blocks.text: ||All 33 Underwater Discoveries are needed. PowerPyx says they are Kenton's shipwrecks, so all seven sets have to be dived even though only five sets count.||

blocks.title: Challenges to finish
blocks.text: ||Leave the 80 challenges for last and skip the 10 slowest. Avoid cheats until the checklist is done: PowerPyx says using one switches off trophies and saving.||

pages.title: Missables and Points of No Return

blocks.text: Missables and
blocks.sub: What closes, and what only seems to

blocks.text: Nothing on the checklist can be lost for good, by PowerPyx's and GTABase's account. A trophy, some optional tasks and a little money can.

blocks.title: The checklist is safe
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and GTABase both say every checklist line can still be done in free roam after the story.||

blocks.title: The one missable trophy
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's trophy guide names Positive Mental Attitude as potentially missable: the meditation at Jason's house cannot be used after Chapter 1, and it is not yet confirmed whether that spot is needed.||

blocks.title: No replays
blocks.text: ||There is no mission replay or chapter select. PowerPyx suggests keeping manual saves at the start and end of each chapter.||

blocks.title: Chapter breaks
blocks.text: ||Points of no return: Recalibration and Tourist Trap in Chapter 1, Checking Out at the end of Chapter 2, The Cartel Heist at the end of Chapter 3. PowerPyx says the last two each need the chapter's other main missions done first.||

blocks.title: Gang operations refill slowly
blocks.text: ||They respawn, but slowly, so take every key valuable on the first visit.||

blocks.caption: What closes, and when
rows: This is a Free Call From...
||Away for a while, back by Chapter 3||

items: ||GTABase tags Bad Driver, This is a Free Call From... and Get Your Wheels as counting toward 100%. No guide read says whether a missed one can ever be made up, only that 100 optional tasks are enough.||

blocks.text: Money for
blocks.sub: What it costs and where it comes from

blocks.text: There is no business to buy or run in Leonida. Money comes from robberies and stolen cars, and the checklist itself earns most of what it costs.

blocks.caption: Costs the guides name on the way to 100%
rows: ||No: trucks can be followed without one||
||Buying is one way; enemies drop them too||
Save for the Future top tier

blocks.title: No businesses
blocks.text: ||TheSixthAxis's review says garages are the only property for sale. No guide read describes a business that earns money on its own.||

blocks.title: The checklist pays for itself
blocks.text: ||The four fencing lines alone mean selling $650,000 of goods: $100,000 of narcotics, $100,000 of jewelry, $250,000 of marked bills and $200,000 of vehicles.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason selling a stash bag in Brian's lockup

blocks.title: Fastest money: vaults
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx calls large bank vaults the fastest earner, up to $205,000 for about five minutes' work, from the end of Chapter 4. VGC also calls bank robberies the largest payout.||

blocks.title: Before the vaults
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's best earners by chapter: Moses' car sales in Chapter 2 ($1,000 or more each); jewelry stores ($10,000 to $25,000), Pay 'n' Spray sales (about $4,000) and Randy's list ($30,000 or more) in Chapter 3. VGC puts Moses at about $1,000 to $5,000 a car.||

blocks.title: Keep it in the bank
blocks.text: ||Bank cash at an ATM. Carried cash is lost when you are Wasted or Busted, and Chapter 1 money is lost at the chapter's end.||

items: ||Total entry fees for the 30 races and the cost of 50 standard weapons: no allowed guide gives a total.||

blocks.text: Trophies and
blocks.sub: What the checklist earns on the way

blocks.text: One trophy is the checklist itself. Many others fall out of it if you follow the route.

blocks.caption: Trophies that come with the checklist. Requirements as the trophy list words them; the last column compares them with the checklist counts.
rows: ||Gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges||
||Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location||
||Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang||

blocks.title: A Long Road
blocks.text: ||The gold trophy A Long Road is awarded for 100% completion. PowerPyx calls it the hardest trophy, and GTABase the last one most players will earn.||

blocks.title: The platinum
blocks.text: ||The platinum, Vice Got a Price!, needs every other trophy, including some outside the checklist such as Strangers & Freaks and Supply & Demand. PowerPyx puts the whole list at about 200 hours.||

blocks.title: Cheats, not cash
blocks.text: ||Challenge groups reward vehicle spawn cheats, which appear in the Progress menu after the story. Using a cheat switches off trophies and saving, so keep them for after 100%.||

items: ||Any in-game reward for reaching 100% beyond the trophy: PowerPyx, GTABase and Push Square name none.||

blocks.text: Master
blocks.sub: Tick it off line by line

blocks.text: One line per item on the 100% checklist, with the chapter of this guide that covers it. Check your own count under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion once the story is done.

blocks.caption: Story & Tasks
Exploration & Activities
Discovery

cover.caption: The 'Just Like Paradise' title over a fishing boat in the mangrove channels of Key Lento

chapters.title: Bank Jobs
chapters.intro: Every bank in Leonida that counts toward 100%: how bank jobs open, how to take a small branch and a vault, and the 22 banks chain by chain.

blocks.text: Bank jobs
blocks.sub: Small branches, big vaults and marked bills

blocks.text: Rockstar showed bank robbery in its trailers long before launch. ||Launch guides count 22 banks to rob for 100%: 14 small branches and 8 large banks with a vault. This page covers what every bank job has in common; the pages after it go bank by bank.||

blocks.caption: ||What you need, as PowerPyx and GTABase list it. Small banks open with the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check; vaults open with the late Chapter 4 optional mission That's Where The Money Is.||
rows: Bank cash is marked bills; a fence takes them only once you have it
Hides your face; put it on from the Items tab before going in
Blow a locked back door or a safe if you have no code
Credit Check desk; PowerPyx also points to Ammu-Nation
A second bag, a getaway driver, or someone to split the police
A vault brings four stars at once

blocks.title: Unlock small banks
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and GTABase say bank jobs open after the Chapter 3 main mission Credit Check (Meet Raul's Crew), which gives the Dye Pack Jammer. PowerPyx puts this about halfway through the story. VGC says the same mission is where you rob a bank alongside a prominent side character before the jammer is yours. GTA BOOM puts small banks at about $5,000 to $45,000 from mid-Chapter 3.||

blocks.title: Find them on the map
blocks.text: ||As the map is uncovered, banks appear as green bank icons. PowerPyx and GTABase give the filter as Map, Robberies (the money bag), Bank Jobs: a finished bank turns bright green, an unfinished one stays dark green, and hovering over an icon shows which of its objectives are still open.||

blocks.title: Read the card before you go
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says selecting a target on the map shows whether it has a safe, its security level from low to high and roughly what the goods are worth. GamesRadar+ says the hover card for a bank shows the potential score and any key valuables, and warns that a bigger score usually means a more dangerous job.||

blocks.title: Three things to take
blocks.text: ||VGC splits a bank into cash drawers, which a threatened teller opens, a safe holding a large number of marked bills, and the vault, which holds the most. PowerPyx says a small bank counts once its cash drawer and its safe are both looted; a large bank has a vault as well, and that too is needed for the checklist.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason inside a Fleeca branch, the front counter on the left and an office desk ahead

blocks.title: Safe codes
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says a safe code can be written somewhere on the premises, such as a note on a board in the back office, or carried by a guard you have put down; Focus Mode (L3 and R3) helps spot it. You can also aim at an employee and choose Threaten or Safe Code?. In Credit Check, PowerPyx has the teller give the code. With no code, PowerPyx and GTABase blow the safe with an explosive.||

blocks.title: Marked bills and fences
blocks.text: ||GTABase says bank and payday loan money comes as marked bills, worth nothing until a fence launders it. PowerPyx and GTABase both name Yasmani in Little Cuba as the best payer for marked bills. PC Gamer says Brian, Donnie and Dunk take goods through drop boxes and pay later, Tyrone and Yasmani pay on the spot, and after two Payday Loan jobs for Yasmani you can leave goods in a garage for pickup for an extra fee.||

blocks.title: Use the pair
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's Credit Check walkthrough shows three partner moves: tell the partner to wait in the driver's seat for a quick getaway, switch to the other character when one bag is full (looting is faster with a single bag), and split up after the job to divide the police.||

blocks.title: Rob quietly for the profile
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says the Professional criminal profile comes from stealth, harming no one in robberies, destroying tapes and disabling alarms. In Credit Check, PowerPyx and GTABase suggest knocking a guard's gun away or shooting his knees rather than killing him.||

blocks.title: Bank jobs in the story
blocks.text: ||Three main missions take you into banks: Credit Check robs three Fleeca branches, and Sinfrontera National Bank scouts the target of The Cartel Heist. PowerPyx has you use Focus in the Sinfrontera mission to inspect the security cameras above the counter. Those missions are done with the story; the 22 bank jobs are separate.||

blocks.title: What goes wrong
items: ||PC Gamer says bank jobs and payday loans have a lot of security and many chances for someone to panic and hit the alarm.||
||VGC says the police response to a bank is huge as soon as they are called, so plan the escape before going in.||
||PowerPyx says any vault robbery brings four wanted stars at once.||
||Which bank jobs, if any, the three Fleeca robberies in Credit Check count toward. No guide read says.||
||Whether a large bank's cash drawer and safe can be robbed before its vault opens. Guides list all three for large banks but do not say.||
||Camera positions inside the 22 banks, and whether their footage can be destroyed. TheSixthAxis says security footage can be deleted in general; no allowed guide covers banks.||
||What wanted level a small bank brings. Guides give four stars only for vaults.||

blocks.text: Small banks,

||No guide read walks through the 14 small banks one by one. The nearest thing is Credit Check, the story mission that teaches bank jobs across three Fleeca branches. These steps follow PowerPyx's and GTABase's walkthroughs of it.||
On the map: 14 bank jobs

blocks.caption: ||The three Fleeca branches in Credit Check as PowerPyx describes them. It does not say which of the guide's two Ocean Beach Fleeca listings each one is.||
rows: Guards in the hall; four marked cash drawers behind the counter
Small; a back door to the back room with a small safe
The largest; more guards, four drawers, a rear security exit
Goes off; security comes from the back

blocks.title: Park for the exit
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx parks outside each branch and, at the last one, on the pavement facing the road for a faster escape. GTABase says the same: park facing the road for a clean exit.||
blocks.frameAlt: A green Fleeca branch seen across the road from the driver's seat of a parked car
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games

blocks.title: Mask on, partner in the car
blocks.text: ||Put the mask on from the Items tab of the inventory before going in. At the second branch the game teaches the hold prompt that tells your partner to wait in the driver's seat, and you go in alone.||

blocks.title: Threaten the guards first
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says to threaten the guards straight away, before they draw. If one does draw, disarm him, shoot him in the knees or use melee. At the biggest branch the guards draw quickly but drop their weapons if you are fast.||

blocks.title: The teller and the cash drawers
blocks.text: ||Threaten the teller: PowerPyx says the teller gives the safe code and can open the cash drawer. Then go behind the counter and take everything around it. The first and third branches have four marked drawers, and PowerPyx says all four are needed there.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason at the front counter of a Fleeca branch, a teller behind it

blocks.title: Through the back door
blocks.text: ||At the small branch the safe is behind a back door. With the alarm cut, PowerPyx says you can plant an explosive on the door, step aside and set it off, or open it with the Snap Gun, or break it.||

blocks.title: The back-room safe
blocks.text: ||Enter the teller's code on the small safe in the back room, or plant an explosive on it. PC Gamer adds that a code may be on a note in the back office or on a downed guard.||

blocks.title: The alarm
blocks.text: ||In Credit Check Karim cuts the alarm at the first two branches. At the third it goes off during the robbery and security comes from the back. PowerPyx says to deal with them and leave at once without trying the safe, as the police are already coming.||
blocks.frameAlt: Karim at a desk of monitors showing maps and plans

blocks.title: Get away
blocks.text: ||Run to the car; PowerPyx says your partner brings it round to face you on the passenger side. Keep clear of the police search zone around a bank you have just robbed. After the last branch, split up with your partner to draw the police apart.||

items: ||Whether every small bank has the same layout as these three Fleecas: back door, back-room safe, drawers behind the counter. No guide read describes the other branches inside.||
||Where cameras are in small banks. No allowed guide marks them.||

blocks.text: Bank vaults,

||The vaults of the eight large banks are the best money in the game, PowerPyx says up to $205,000 a time. A vault only opens while a security van's guard is delivering cash, so every vault job starts on the road.||
On the map: 8 big bank jobs

blocks.caption: ||What you need for a vault job, from PowerPyx and GTABase.||
rows: That's Where The Money Is... done
The late Chapter 4 optional mission from Yasmani that opens vaults
Needed before he sells van tips
A tip marks security vans with a purple icon
To blow the doorway at the back of the bank
More bags than one character can carry; a driver
A fast motorcycle, a hat and glasses
For four stars and the clean-up afterwards

blocks.title: Unlock the vaults
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and GTABase say Yasmani gets in touch after the Chapter 4 mission VCIA Takedown with That's Where The Money Is... (Wait at the Cafe), for Jason or Lucia. PowerPyx calls it an endgame feature at the very end of Chapter 4; its fence guide instead says Chapter 5. Vaults can still be robbed after the story.||

blocks.title: Wait at the cafe
blocks.text: ||For the first job, go into Cafe Orquidea in Ocean Beach and sit at a window seat until the security van drives past.||
blocks.frameAlt: The Cafe Orquidea Cuban Restaurant sign

blocks.title: Find a van later
blocks.text: ||After the mission PowerPyx gives three ways: follow security vans you come across, wait at a bank until one arrives, or pay Yasmani $10,000 for a tip, which marks the vans with a purple icon. GTABase lists Tail the Security Van as a Yasmani mission needed for 100%.||
blocks.frameAlt: A Gruppe 6 armoured van with its doors open and two motorcycles beside it
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games

blocks.title: Tail it at a distance
blocks.text: ||Get in a vehicle and follow the van from a distance; PowerPyx and GTABase both say the driver notices if you get too close. It stops outside a bank.||

blocks.title: Follow the guard in
blocks.text: ||Park nearby and follow the guard into the bank on foot. PowerPyx says he carries a briefcase of cash into the vault, which is open only while he does. Inside, put on a disguise and draw your gun.||

blocks.title: Blow the back doorway
blocks.text: ||Plant explosives on the doorway at the back of the room to open it. Guards wait inside the vault; deal with them before going on.||

blocks.title: Fill both bags
blocks.text: ||The marked bills are piled on a cart in a corner of the vault, usually more than two bags hold. Hand a full bag to your partner (hold Right on the D-pad and press Circle or B) or switch to them and keep taking. GTABase says a full haul in the first job is worth around $80,000.||

blocks.title: Four stars, front door
blocks.text: ||Robbing the vault brings four stars at once and the police shoot straight away. The bank in the first job has no back exit, so you leave through the front and clear the way. Let your partner drive while you shoot at the cars behind.||

blocks.title: Lose them and change
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and GTABase suggest a fast motorcycle to weave through traffic. A highway helps in a fast car, but expect roadblocks. Once out of sight, pull into a parking lot, swap vehicles, take off the disguise and put on a hat and glasses.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia aiming a rifle as a rider on a red motorcycle passes a security van

blocks.title: Sell to Yasmani
blocks.text: ||Take the money to Yasmani to sell. PowerPyx's endgame loop is to drop the cash at Yasmani's or at a garage for him to collect, then do the next vault; it puts the rate at about $100,000 to $200,000 every five minutes.||

blocks.caption: ||A vault job from start to finish, as PowerPyx and GTABase describe the first one.||

||Out the front with four stars||

blocks.title: Two trophies on the way
blocks.text: ||Push Square and PC Gamer list Maximum Withdrawal for robbing five bank vaults and escaping. PowerPyx says A Classic Blitz Play, for robbing an armoured truck and escaping, can unlock during That's Where The Money Is.||

blocks.caption: Masked robbers holding up the crew of a Gruppe 6 armoured van.

chapters.title: Robberies, Raids & Fences
chapters.intro: Every robbery the 100% list asks for except banks: stores, pawn shops, jewelry stores, payday loans, ATMs, gang operations and stolen cars, with the way in, the code, the way out and who buys the take.

blocks.text: Robberies
blocks.sub: The 100% Guide

blocks.text: Every robbery the 100% checklist asks for, apart from banks and vaults, which have their own chapter. This page sets the targets side by side and gives the routine that works for nearly all of them.

blocks.caption: Lucia and Jason going into a store with their faces covered, in Rockstar's first trailer.
||What the checklist asks for. Counts are from PowerPyx's and Push Square's 100% lists; takes are PowerPyx's per robbery, except where stated.||

blocks.text: The routine

blocks.title: Read the card first
blocks.text: ||Every target sits in the map's Robberies tab. GTABase says jewelry stores, pawn shops, banks and payday loans show an estimated take there, and PowerPyx says hovering over a gang operation shows how many key valuables it holds.||

blocks.title: Cover your face
blocks.text: ||Buy a mask, then set its Wear Style so it covers your face: PC Gamer says hold L1, press R1 to reach items, pick the mask and press Up. GTABase's police guide says put it on before the crime and take it off once out of sight; changing outfit or hair also clears the appearance icon.||
blocks.frameAlt: The item wheel with a neck gaiter mask switched on

blocks.title: Bring help and a way out
blocks.text: ||From Coffee Break on you can switch between Jason and Lucia and give the other orders, and GTABase says robbing together helps their relationship. PC Gamer says two people carry more bags. PowerPyx suggests a fast sports bike for losing the police.||

blocks.title: Go in the back where you can
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says the Snap Gun from Chapter 3 picks door locks without setting off alarms, so a back door lets you reach staff, the footage and the alarm before anyone out front knows. GTABase says kicking doors in or blowing safes brings a heavy police response and less time.||

blocks.title: Deal with the cameras
blocks.text: ||GTABase says CCTV recorded on site can be destroyed, so the police cannot use it to identify you. Footage kept in the cloud cannot be removed, and an alarm eventually goes off anyway.||

blocks.title: Switch the alarm off
blocks.text: ||VGC says disabling a store's security delays the police. PC Gamer says that with the alarm off and your partner keeping the room under control, you can empty every case and drawer at your own pace.||

blocks.title: Find the code
blocks.text: ||Codes turn up in several places. VGC says a back-room code can be on a Post-it note nearby, or a threatened employee can be asked for it. In the first Chapter 1 job, GamesRadar+ says the clerk gives the code if you do not hit him in the face. GTA BOOM found one in an email on a computer.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason facing a shop clerk with his hands raised

blocks.title: Enter it, or force it
blocks.text: ||A code you have learned is shown under Notes on the keypad. Without one, the safe can take a sticky bomb through Plant Explosive, which GamesRadar+ says needs bombs you can buy only after Credit Check in Chapter 3. GTA BOOM says some safes have Break Open: hold Triangle or Y and keep the right stick where the circle fills fastest.||
blocks.frameAlt: A door keypad with the learned code under Notes

blocks.title: Get clear and lose the stars
blocks.text: ||GTABase says break line of sight and keep moving out of the search area; the stars flash before they go, and K9 units keep tracking you. Bags left in the trunk can be lost if you do not escape.||

blocks.title: Turn the bags into money
blocks.text: ||Goods in a stash bag are not money until a fence or drop-off takes them. The Fencing page has who pays what.||

blocks.title: What loses you the take
items: ||Busted or Wasted: GTABase says you lose pocket cash, a small BuckMe fee and most likely any stash bags you carry.||
||The end of Chapter 1: GTA BOOM says cash still carried when the chapter ends is wiped, so bank it first.||
||Needless violence: GTABase says threats do not hurt the criminal profile but unnecessary violence does.||

blocks.text: Tools and
Most robbery tools come from story missions, not shops. This is the order they arrive in, and what each one opens.

blocks.title: Buy a mask before the first job
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says the earliest mask is sold at Chuck's Tackle & Shot, just down the road from Jason's house in Key Lento: turn right inside, then left down the aisle to the Neckwear shelf. Most Ammu-Nation stores stock them too.||

blocks.text: ||Stick ups and gang operations are open from the start. Brian takes goods after Lab Fees and Donnie after Clean Up After Donnie.||

blocks.text: ||The mission Moses gives the Slim Jim and makes Moses a buyer for cars with no tracker.||

blocks.text: ||VGC says Coffee Break unlocks free switching between the two leads and four jobs that can be done in any order: Thrillbillies, Hit Avery Pawn, Hit Kingpin Bowling and Impounded Vehicle. PowerPyx says pawn shops open as robberies from here.||

blocks.title: Chapter 2: Slam Dunk
blocks.text: ||Dunk becomes a fence in Port Gellhorn, and the next day he calls and marks two robbery locations.||

blocks.title: Chapter 3: Yasmani and the Snap Gun
blocks.text: ||Boobie Time brings Yasmani. His Jewelry Jobs hand over the Snap Gun and open the jewelry stores; Here, Kitty Kitty makes Tyrone a buyer.||

blocks.title: Chapter 3: Credit Check
blocks.text: ||Credit Check gives the Dye Pack Jammer and opens payday loan stores and small banks. GamesRadar+ says sticky bombs can be bought at Ammu-Nation from this point.||

blocks.text: ||This mission gives the Key Cloner and makes Randy a buyer for high-end cars.||

blocks.text: Stick
Convenience stores, liquor stores, fast food joints and gas station shops. Small takes, little police, and 50 different ones count toward 100%.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||A gun, a mask and nothing else. Stick ups are open from Chapter 1.||

blocks.title: Pick 50 different stores
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's checklist asks for 50 of the 91 stores the map tracks; doing the same store twice does not add to it. Its progress database lists 72 convenience stores, 14 liquor stores and 23 fast food joints, which adds up to 109, so its two pages disagree.||

blocks.title: Mask up at the door
blocks.text: ||Put the mask on before you walk in and take it off once you are out of sight. Most small stores have cameras, and recorded footage can be used to identify you.||

blocks.title: Aim at the cashier
blocks.text: ||VGC says hold L2 to aim at the cashier without firing; GamesRadar+ says press Square or X while aiming at staff to demand the register cash. The cashier opens the register.||

blocks.title: Check for a back room
blocks.text: ||VGC says some stores keep a safe in the back. Kick the door in, make the employee open it, ask the threatened employee for the code, or look for it on a Post-it note nearby.||

blocks.title: Look for hidden rooms
blocks.text: ||VGC says some stores have secret rooms, often with gang activity behind them. Check the minimap for rooms you have not entered, then pick the lock or find another way in.||

blocks.title: Leave before the police come
blocks.text: ||VGC says the police response to a grocery store is low but they do come, so be gone by then. GTA BOOM says keep the customers down and put the gun away as you leave.||

blocks.caption: ||What a stick up pays. Each guide gives its own range; none gives a figure per store.||
rows: ||A couple of thousand dollars at most||

blocks.title: Two Criminal challenges
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists two challenges for store robberies: three stores in one day, and two stores in each of the five counties within 20 minutes, both without dying or being arrested.||

items: ||Which stores keep a back-room safe. No guide read lists them.||
||Whether a repeated stick up still counts toward the 50. The checklist wording asks for different stores.||

blocks.text: Pawn
Fifteen pawn shops can be robbed from the middle of Chapter 2. With the 20 jewelry stores they make the 35 smash 'n' grabs, of which 34 count toward 100%.
On the map: 5 pawn shops

blocks.caption: Lucia outside Buck's Jewelry & Pawn at dusk.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||A gun and a mask; a partner for the room; a fast bike or a car outside. From Chapter 3 the Snap Gun for back doors and sticky bombs for safes.||

blocks.title: Unlock them
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says pawn shops become robberies after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, about halfway through the chapter. Filter the map with Robberies, the money bag icon, then Smash 'n' Grabs: dark green is not done, bright green is done.||

blocks.title: Scout it first
blocks.text: ||VGC calls pawn shops lucrative but heavily secured, and says many can be entered from the back, where the security can be switched off and the CCTV footage destroyed. These robberies bring a higher wanted level than a grocery store.||

blocks.title: Expect the clerk to fight
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer warns that pawn shop clerks are quick to shoot and will not go down without a fight. Keep your partner on the staff while you work.||

blocks.title: Threaten the staff and smash the cases
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and GTABase say to threaten the staff and smash the display cases for the jewelry. Breaking a case or a door alerts the police and brings two stars.||

blocks.title: Get into the back room
blocks.text: ||The safe is in the back room. The staff may give its code when threatened; otherwise break the door and use a sticky bomb once you have them.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia at a storage shelf in a pawn shop back room

blocks.title: Loot the safe, or it does not count
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says a shop counts as done only once its back-room safe is looted; smashing the cases alone may not be enough.||

blocks.title: Leave and lose the stars
blocks.text: ||Leaving before the police arrive is possible but means less loot. PowerPyx suggests a fast sports bike through traffic, or going off-road.||

blocks.caption: ||The 15 pawn shops in PowerPyx's numbered list, with the take range the game's robbery card gives.||
rows: ||$1,000 to $10,000; also the mission Hit Avery Pawn||

items: ||Guards, camera positions and safe spots for each shop: no guide read describes them shop by shop.||
||The encyclopedia also has Pawn & Gun, Vice City Gun & Pawn and Zenon's Pawn Shop, which are not in PowerPyx's list of robbable shops.||
||Which one of the 35 smash 'n' grabs can be skipped: the checklist asks for 34 without saying.||

blocks.text: Hit Avery
The optional Chapter 2 job that introduces pawn shop robberies, in Port Gellhorn. GTABase marks it as required for 100%.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||Coffee Break done; Jason or Lucia; a gun; a fast bike for the getaway.||

blocks.title: Start it
blocks.text: ||After Coffee Break, Avery Pawn is one of four jobs marked on the map. Either lead can do it.||
blocks.frameAlt: The strip mall in Port Gellhorn with the pawn shop billboard

blocks.title: Threaten the staff
blocks.text: ||Go to the pawn shop in Port Gellhorn and pull your gun on the staff.||

blocks.title: Smash the cases
blocks.text: ||Break the display cases for the jewelry. Breaking a case or a door calls the police and gives two stars.||

blocks.title: Open the safe
blocks.text: ||The staff may give you the safe combination. Break the safe room door, then open the safe. PowerPyx's code was 6499 but it says the code may be randomised, and GTABase says the same, so use the one your game gives.||

blocks.title: Lose the cops
blocks.text: ||Get out of the search area. PowerPyx suggests a fast sports bike through traffic, where the police cannot keep up, or going off-road.||

blocks.title: Fence the bag at Dunk's
blocks.text: ||Selling the jewelry is optional for the mission. Stash the bag at Dunk's trailer in Port Gellhorn to be paid.||

items: ||The payout: both guides say only that it depends on how much you take.||
||Whether the code 6499 is the same in every game.||

blocks.text: Jewelry
Twenty jewelry stores open once Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs are done. They pay the most of any store robbery, and the quiet way in is through the back.
On the map: 36 smash and grabs

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||The Snap Gun; a mask; your partner for crowd control; sticky bombs if you will not find the code.||

blocks.title: Unlock them
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says jewelry stores become robberies after the Chapter 3 mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs, about halfway through the chapter.||

blocks.title: Pick the back door
blocks.text: ||Use the Snap Gun on the back door. PC Gamer says you get in without anyone usually noticing and can quietly deal with any staff or security in the back.||

blocks.title: Destroy the footage
blocks.text: ||Find the security footage in the back and destroy it, so the police get no description of you.||

blocks.title: Switch off the alarm
blocks.text: ||Disable the alarm system at its panel. PC Gamer says that with alarms off you can take your time; VGC says it delays the police.||

blocks.title: Get the safe code
blocks.text: ||GTABase says the code is often in an office or on a desk; PC Gamer says you can also threaten someone for it. Without it, a sticky bomb or kicking doors brings a heavier police response.||

blocks.title: Empty the safe
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says a store counts toward 100% only once its back-room safe is looted.||

blocks.title: Clear the front
blocks.text: ||With your partner keeping the shop floor under control, smash every display case and empty the cash drawers. PC Gamer also takes wallets and the drugs in first-aid kits.||

blocks.title: Slip away
blocks.text: ||Done right, PC Gamer says you can leave clean without a chase. GTABase says a store needs time to restock, so robbing it again soon usually pays less.||

blocks.caption: ||The 20 jewelry stores in PowerPyx's numbered list, with their take ranges.||

items: ||Safe codes for the 17 stores outside Yasmani's jobs: no allowed guide prints them, and they are found in the store each time.||
||Which stores have a back door the Snap Gun opens. PowerPyx and GTABase confirm it only for Richardson and Donovan Banks, and say Casa de Empeno has none.||

blocks.text: Yasmani's
A Chapter 3 mission for either lead: three stores, one wanted piece from each, sold to Yasmani in Little Cuba. It hands over the Snap Gun.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||Boobie Time done; a gun; a mask. The Snap Gun comes after the first delivery.||

blocks.title: Take the job
blocks.text: ||It opens after Boobie Time and starts at Vice City and Ocean Beach Banks. Yasmani wants one piece from each of three stores, in any order.||

blocks.title: Casa de Empeno first
blocks.text: ||Go in by the front door; this shop has no back door for the Snap Gun. The safe is in the small back office, and the security box to its left destroys the video footage. The code is 1680. The piece is a buffalo skull chain; the display cases are extra.||

blocks.title: Deliver the first piece
blocks.text: ||Both guides recommend taking the first piece straight to Yasmani: he hands over the Snap Gun, which makes the other two stores much easier.||

blocks.title: Richardson Jewelry
blocks.text: ||Open the back door with the Snap Gun. Disarm security at the panel to the right of the door into the central room, then destroy the recording at the box under the security screen. The safe is in the north-east corner of the central room; the code is 6815. Take the diamond ring.||

blocks.title: Donovan Banks & Co.
blocks.text: ||Open the back door with the Snap Gun. The footage and the security system are both in the small back office. The safe is halfway down the long back hallway; the code is 0104. Take the amethyst necklace.||

blocks.title: Quiet exit or full sweep
blocks.text: ||At Richardson and Donovan Banks you can leave as soon as the safe is open, or go through to the front and empty the cases for more money.||

blocks.title: Sell to Yasmani
blocks.text: ||Take everything to Yasmani's shop. The requested pieces pay $20,000, plus whatever else you stole; the job also opens garage pickups by Yasmani.||

blocks.caption: ||Safe codes and pieces. PowerPyx and GTABase give the same three codes.||

items: ||Guard counts, the wanted level each store brings and what each store pays on its own: neither guide gives them.||
||Whether these codes stay the same in every game. Both guides print them; at Avery Pawn PowerPyx warns its code may be randomised.||

blocks.text: Payday
Seven payday loan stores, all needed for 100%. They pay in marked bills, so they wait for the Dye Pack Jammer.
On the map: 7 payday loan stores

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||Credit Check done, which gives the Dye Pack Jammer; a gun; a getaway.||

blocks.title: Unlock them
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says payday loans open after the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check (Meet Raul's Crew), about halfway through the story, which also gives the jammer. They show as green hand icons, under Map, Robberies, Payday Loans.||

blocks.title: Threaten the teller
blocks.text: ||Aim your gun at the teller and wait for the cash to be put on the counter, then take it.||

blocks.title: Watch for the panic button
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says payday loans and banks have lots of cash but lots of security, and many chances for someone to panic and hit the alarm.||

blocks.title: Rob the back-room safe
blocks.text: ||Go into the back room and empty the safe. PowerPyx counts a store as fully completed only with both the counter cash and the safe.||

blocks.title: Escape the police
blocks.text: ||Lose your wanted level before going anywhere near a buyer.||

blocks.title: Launder the bills
blocks.text: ||Marked bills can be fenced only once you have the Dye Pack Jammer. Yasmani pays high for them.||

blocks.title: Two for Yasmani
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says that after two payday loan robberies Yasmani sells security van tips for $10,000. PC Gamer says two payday loan jobs for him also let you leave goods in a garage for pickup.||

blocks.caption: ||The seven stores in PowerPyx's list, with its take ranges.||

items: ||Safe codes, guards and camera positions at payday loan stores: the allowed guides read do not describe them.||
||The wanted level a payday loan robbery brings.||

blocks.text: ATMs and
Yasmani's later jobs open two noisy ways to steal marked bills: tearing an ATM out of the wall, and blowing the back off a security van.
On the map: 12 atms

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||A vehicle with a winch; sticky bombs; the Dye Pack Jammer to sell the bills.||

blocks.title: Unlock them
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says ATMs and security trucks open through Yasmani's jobs; its side-mission list names Yasmani's ATM Jobs among them.||

blocks.title: Fit a winch
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says a winch is attached at a Mod Shop. PC Gamer says to put it on a truck.||

blocks.title: Pull the ATM out
blocks.text: ||Hook the ATM and drag it out of the wall.||

blocks.title: Open it
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says to shoot the security cases to get the cash. PC Gamer says the machine itself has to be smashed or blown open first, then each cash container broken.||

blocks.title: Expect company
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer calls it noisy, slow work that draws police in numbers. Have the escape route planned.||

blocks.title: Security vans
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says sticky bombs on a security truck's back door blow it open. After his Chapter 3 jobs, sticky bombs are found at the back of Yasmani's shop.||

blocks.title: Van tips and vaults
blocks.text: ||The vans Yasmani sells tips on lead to bank vaults, which the bank chapter covers.||

items: ||How much an ATM or a van holds.||
||Whether ATMs or vans count toward 100%: neither checklist read lists them.||

blocks.text: Gang
Thirty-nine hideouts, fronts and labs run by nine gangs and groups. Every one has to be cleared for 100%, and clearing means every key valuable.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||Armor, healing and a rifle; a suppressed weapon for a quiet approach; sticky bombs for safes from Chapter 3; a car with trunk space for the bags.||

blocks.title: Find them
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says an operation is marked with a yellow icon once you enter its area. Until visited it reads Robbery Opportunity; after that it shows its name. Filter with Map, Robberies, Illegal Operations. Progress, Gangs counts what you have found and finished per gang.||

blocks.title: Count the valuables
blocks.text: ||Hover over the icon to see how many key valuables the site holds: usually a unique weapon variant, a luxury watch and a safe with cash. PowerPyx says 19 sites are marked by the story.||

blocks.title: Choose loud or quiet
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says to expect a major gunfight or a long, risky stealth approach. GTA BOOM went in quietly at Watson Bay with a suppressed pistol.||

blocks.title: Take every key valuable
blocks.text: ||A site counts only when every key valuable is taken. Narcotics are extra: VGC says weed is cheap while crystal and cocaine are worth far more, and that drugs have to be carried to a buyer.||

blocks.title: Open the safe
blocks.text: ||Safes here open with a code found on site, a sticky bomb, or Break Open: hold Triangle or Y and keep the right stick where the circle fills.||

blocks.title: Carry it out
blocks.text: ||Store the bags in your vehicle and come back for more. GTA BOOM found a van full of cocaine at one site.||

blocks.title: Come back later
blocks.text: ||A cleared site greys out and restocks after a long while. GTA BOOM found that some loot does not come back, so the first visit pays best.||

blocks.caption: ||Operations per gang, from PowerPyx's numbered list.||

blocks.title: Pest Control
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says robbing one operation of each gang earns the Pest Control trophy.||

items: ||Cash in each safe and guard counts per site: no allowed guide gives them for most sites.||

blocks.text: Kingpin
The Kolts' bowling alley in Port Gellhorn, one of the four Coffee Break jobs in Chapter 2. Three key valuables, a safe with a known code, and a trophy.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||Your partner; body armor; five Zombix; a rifle. The safe code, or a sticky bomb.||

blocks.title: Start it
blocks.text: ||It is marked after Coffee Break in Chapter 2, at Kingpin Bowling in Port Gellhorn, Kelly County. Either lead can take it.||
blocks.frameAlt: The parking lot of Kingpin Bowling with its letter signs on the roof

blocks.title: Gear up
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says call your partner to you, buy five Zombix at a convenience store and refill your armor at Ammu-Nation's counter.||

blocks.title: Fight your way in
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says to shoot your way in: there are many Kolts inside. GamesRadar+ and VGC warn of the same at Brooks Boatworks.||

blocks.title: Take the watch and the shotgun
blocks.text: ||The luxury watch is in the south-east room. The Gutterball Moreland 850 lies on the pool table in the north-east corner.||

blocks.title: Spare sticky bombs
blocks.text: ||VGC found sticky bombs on a table behind the lanes, where the pins are dispensed, and says the game often leaves some near a safe. It could not say whether they always appear.||
blocks.frameAlt: A Sticky Bomb pickup in a crate on a workbench

blocks.title: Open the office safe
blocks.text: ||The safe is in the small north-east office. The code is 0300, and you can enter it without finding it first. The clue by the safe points to Brooks Boatworks, where the code is on a map pinned in an upstairs office; GamesRadar+ says that map also has two other safe codes.||
blocks.frameAlt: The office safe with Plant Explosive and Enter Code prompts

blocks.title: Or blow it
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says use sticky bombs on the safe. GamesRadar+ notes Plant Explosive stays greyed out until you have bombs, which Ammu-Nation sells only from Credit Check in Chapter 3.||

blocks.title: Get out
blocks.text: ||Leave by the alley with two stars, find a vehicle and drive off. Looting all three valuables and escaping unlocks Let's Go Bowling, though the trophy can pop late.||

blocks.title: Missed something?
blocks.text: ||The job cannot be missed: PowerPyx says the alley restocks in Chapter 3 for anything you left.||
Watson Bay
A high-security La Polilla Negra house by the water. GTA BOOM's guide follows one quiet run as Lucia; its details are one player's game.

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||A suppressed weapon and a plan to leave by water. GTA BOOM did not test whether the site opens earlier in the story.||

blocks.title: Find it
blocks.text: ||Look for the gold moth marker at the end of a short spur off the coast road, across the water from the built-up shore. The map rates it High security with a take value of $2,700 to $4,700. GTABase places it just east of Watson Bay.||

blocks.title: Skip the gate
blocks.text: ||Follow the water along the outside of the fence and climb the blue tarp over the metal bars. Use the buildings as cover.||

blocks.title: Guards
blocks.text: ||One guard stands under the stairs and two at the rear. Check both sides of the driveway gate; the white shed by the pool gives cover.||

blocks.title: Into the house
blocks.text: ||From the pool, face the house, take the outdoor stairs on the right and go in by the white glass-paned door. Check the rooms before looting.||

blocks.title: The valuables
blocks.text: ||The La Polilla Negra VF-G1 is in a black hard case on the wooden table under the window, in the room off the kitchen. Cocaine is on the kitchen counter and a B&G Ark Royal Quantum watch on the desk by the monitors. Grenades and sticky bombs are in a box near the shelving, and a modified pickup is in the garage.||

blocks.title: The safe and its code
blocks.text: ||The safe is under the microwave beside the kitchen window. The code is the last line of an email on the kitchen desktop computer; in GTA BOOM's game it was 1819. Choose Enter Code.||

blocks.title: The take
blocks.text: ||GTA BOOM found $877 and $2,104 in cash, $2,981 in all, plus about $720 of goods in the bag that must be fenced. The take value on the map is not the cash figure.||

blocks.title: Escape
blocks.text: ||If the road is clear, open the gate with the control by the driveway. If not, go back over the fence at the blue tarp, follow the shore to a wooden dock, swim the North Heron River and lose the stars in the mangroves.||

items: ||Whether the safe code is the same in every game: GTA BOOM does not say.||
||The wanted level the raid brings.||

blocks.text: More
Four more illegal operations with something written about them by an allowed guide: two early ones, a warehouse full of cocaine, and the Ultimate Edition's extra.
On the map: 3 kitty litter lab raids
Apollo Aggregates

blocks.title: Find the warehouse
blocks.text: ||GTA BOOM puts the red Apollo Aggregates warehouse east of Hamlet in South Vice-Dale County, past the three rectangular pools beside the highway. Drive through the gravel yard past the striped barrier.||

blocks.title: Break in at the side
blocks.text: ||Break open the grey side door beside the Apollo trailer. A box of cash sits outside it.||

blocks.title: Load up
blocks.text: ||A stash bag of $6,000 in marked bills is on the table near the middle. Cocaine is in the back of the teddy-bear van inside, on tables in the first office and in the safe; a second van in the yard reads Cocaine (Full). Bag it, store it in your vehicle and come back.||

blocks.title: Break the office safe
blocks.text: ||The safe sits on a filing cabinet by the lockers in the second office. Hold Triangle or Y for Break Open, move the right stick until the circle fills fast and hold it there. Inside are cash, cocaine and a Leroy Rook card.||

blocks.title: Sell it
blocks.text: ||For one full haul Donnie quoted $14,400, $8,400 for the narcotics and $6,000 for the bills, and Brian $12,720. Donnie pays into the mailbox at Jason's house after he texts.||
Fishing Shacks

blocks.title: An early Kingfishers site
blocks.text: ||GTA BOOM names the Kingfishers fishing shacks as an early raid paying about $1,000 to $2,000 once fully looted. GTABase places them in Wetman Bay, the swamp south-west of Hamlet, with the Kingfishers W-22.||
Stash House

blocks.title: Kolts in north Port Gellhorn
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists the Stash House as the fifth Kolts & Associates site. GTABase places it in north Port Gellhorn, a little east of Brooks Boatworks, with the Kolt & Associates 556 to loot.||
Illegal Goods (Ultimate Edition)

blocks.title: The bonus robberies
blocks.text: ||Push Square says they open from Chapter 1 once you have visited South Vice-Dale County, around SW 13th St and El Joven Blvd in Southside. Beat the gang inside, take the jewelry and drugs before the police come, drive off and fence the goods. PowerPyx says the site is not needed for 100%.||

items: ||The Stash House's layout, guards and safe: the allowed guides read describe only where it is.||
||Which gang holds Apollo Aggregates and whether it is one of the 39.||

blocks.text: Fencing
Jewelry, narcotics and marked bills are worth nothing until a fence takes them. Five fences buy goods; who pays best depends on what you carry.

blocks.caption: Lucia counting banknotes in a car, in Rockstar's first trailer.

blocks.title: Know what you are carrying
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says illegal operations give jewelry, marked bills, narcotics and pocket cash; smash and grabs, banks and payday loans give jewelry, marked bills and pocket cash. Goods go in a stash bag, and the bag goes in the trunk.||

blocks.title: Lose the stars first
blocks.text: ||GTABase says clear your wanted level before going to a buyer.||

blocks.title: Compare the rates
blocks.text: ||Hover over a fence on the map to see what it pays for each kind of goods, from Very Low to Very High. The Robberies section of the Index lists the fences open to you under Drop-offs, Goods.||

blocks.title: Drop it off
blocks.text: ||Brian, Donnie and Dunk take goods into a drop box: Brian's Lockup, opened with the door code 7700, a box at Donnie's trailer, and the trunk of Dunk's car. Tyrone and Yasmani pay on the spot, at Tyrone's apartment and Yasmani's shop.||

blocks.title: Wait for the money
blocks.text: ||Drop box money comes later. PowerPyx says early in Chapter 1 it arrives in the mailbox outside Jason's home, and by bank transfer once he has a bank account. GamesRadar+ says it can take several days, and Brian may hold a payment until you do his next mission.||

blocks.title: Use a garage later
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says that from Chapter 3, once Yasmani is a fence, goods can be left at a garage and a fence chosen to collect them. PC Gamer ties it to two payday loan jobs for Yasmani and says it costs an extra fee; VGC says buyers who collect take a larger cut.||

blocks.title: Or send your partner
blocks.text: ||With both leads together, put the bag in your car, hold Right and choose Fence Goods; the option does not always show. PC Gamer says the partner gets a little less than you would.||

blocks.caption: ||Rates are the game's own, as PowerPyx lists them; unlock missions from PC Gamer and GTABase.||

blocks.title: Brian or Donnie?
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ priced the same cocaine haul at $3,400 from Donnie and $2,720 from Brian, but still suggests selling late Chapter 1 hauls to Brian, as Cal advises.||

blocks.title: Fences that go away
items: ||PowerPyx says Brian is not available after Chapter 1, Donnie not after the Chapter 1 mission Swamped, and Dunk is away for part of the story. Tyrone, Yasmani and Dunk stay open after the story.||

blocks.text: Stolen
Cars are fenced to three kinds of buyer, chosen by the tracker the car carries. $200,000 of vehicle sales counts toward 100%.
On the map: 7 vehicle thefts for moses

blocks.title: What you need
blocks.text: ||The WAiNK app on the phone; the Slim Jim from the mission Moses; later the Key Cloner.||

blocks.title: Scan before you steal
blocks.text: ||Open the phone with Up and use WAiNK. GTA BOOM says the scan shows the security level, the tool needed, the tracker tier, the registration cost and the resale value.||
blocks.frameAlt: A scan card showing a standard tracker, sale value and registration cost

blocks.title: Moses: no tracker
blocks.text: ||Moses, in Port Gellhorn from Chapter 2, takes only cars without a tracker, and not ones stolen close to his garage; GTABase says steal a few streets away. PC Gamer says he wants older, low-profile cars.||
blocks.frameAlt: A parked car marked as suitable to take to Moses Watkins

blocks.title: Get in quietly
blocks.text: ||Use the Slim Jim on locked or alarmed cars. GTA BOOM says smashing a window can set the alarm off.||

blocks.title: Keep it clean
blocks.text: ||Damage lowers the price, so drive carefully on the way.||

blocks.title: Get paid
blocks.text: ||Hover over Moses' shop on the map to check the price, then talk to him and take the payment. He usually pays $1,000 or more. After a sale there is a wait before he takes another: PowerPyx says about two minutes, VGC says sleeping at a safehouse ends it.||
blocks.frameAlt: A car pulling up to the open door of Watkins Auto Parts

blocks.title: Pay 'n' Spray: standard tracker
blocks.text: ||From early Chapter 3 any of the 19 Pay 'n' Spray shops takes cars with a standard tracker. PowerPyx's 100% guide says about $2,500 or more in perfect condition; its money guide says around $4,000.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia beside a red sports car whose card shows it registered

blocks.title: Randy: the wish list
blocks.text: ||After Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS gives the Key Cloner, Randy in Balsero buys high-end cars with advanced trackers from his wish list, about $35,000 or more each in perfect condition. GTA BOOM says higher trackers report the car to police if you slow down for too long, and GTABase says lose any tail before the drop.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia at a car door with the Clone Key prompt

blocks.title: Finish the list
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's trophy guide counts 16 cars and its money guide 18. Finishing Randy's last job earns Supply & Demand, and every delivery to Moses or Randy is one of the 100 optional tasks.||

blocks.caption: ||Moses' six requests in PowerPyx's order, with the pay it saw. They come one at a time.||
rows: ||Bastion St, south-west Port Gellhorn, being towed||
||A lockup at the Draper Island Docks||
||A driveway on Orchard Avenue, south Port Gellhorn||
||Driven by a group in Buckskin Swamp, south-east Kelly County||
||A shed north-east of Grayson; keypad code 2727, on signs in the trailer nearby||
||The Final Chapter gang site in Ambrosia||

items: ||How many cars can be sold in a day.||
||Whether a single car can be both registered and sold for the checklist.||

blocks.text: Other
Robberies that are not on a map list: other crews' loot, an armoured van with Billy, Dunk's tips, and the small change in trunks and on rooftops.
On the map: 3 dunn's robbery tips

blocks.title: Rob the robbers
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer calls it the best advice it has: when you hear sirens, alarms or gunshots, find the crew fleeing with duffel bags, drop them and take the bags. It puts the take at $1,000 to $15,000. The heat that was on them moves to you, so leave fast, and come as a pair to carry every bag.||

blocks.title: The armoured van
blocks.text: ||In Billy's Chapter 2 job Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab, his crew stops a Gruppe 6 armoured van. Shoot it until it crashes, plant the charge on the back doors and step well back, or you can kill the crew and fail. Keep the guard covered while Billy bags the cash.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason walking away as the charge on the van goes off

blocks.title: Follow Billy out
blocks.text: ||Ride after Billy off-road, over a river jump, under a bridge and through tunnels, until the police give up. The bag holds $3,000, of which Jason gets $2,000, and the dirt bike can then be called through ScooterBros.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason in a helmet on a dirt bike in tall grass

blocks.title: Dunk's tips
blocks.text: ||The day after Slam Dunk, Dunk calls and marks two robbery locations. PowerPyx lists Dunk's Robbery Tips as a Chapter 3 strand but has no walkthrough for it.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason talking with Dunk in a shop

blocks.title: Police car trunks
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says breaking into a cruiser with the Slim Jim unlocks its trunk, which often holds a rifle, a shotgun or armor; a screwdriver opens it but sets the alarm off. Police pickups have a crate in the bed with no alarm.||

blocks.title: Small change
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer finds lockboxes with a little cash on most rooftops, drugs or cash in car trunks, and cocaine in boats washed up on the coast. Mugging pays a couple of hundred dollars at most.||

items: ||What Dunk's tips lead to: the guides read do not name the two places beyond a trailer area in Lost Vista, Port Gellhorn.||
||Whether any of these count toward 100%.||

blocks.text: Robbery
Everything on this chapter's pages that counts toward 100%, with the counts the two checklists read give.

blocks.caption: ||Items from PowerPyx's and Push Square's 100% lists that this chapter covers. Bank jobs, vaults and their marked bills are in the bank chapter.||
rows: ||100; each car delivered to Moses or Randy is one||

blocks.caption: ||Trophies tied to these pages, from PowerPyx.||
rows: ||Rob one illegal operation of each gang||
||Take all three valuables at Kingpin Bowling and escape||

blocks.title: Order that saves time
blocks.text: ||Do stick ups and gang operations as you pass them in Chapter 1, but bank the cash before the chapter ends. Sell cars to Moses from Chapter 2. Hold jewelry for Yasmani's high rate in Chapter 3, and leave payday loans until Credit Check gives the jammer.||

chapters.title: Missions
chapters.intro: Every story mission in order, chapter by chapter, and every contact who hands out side work: who sends you, where it starts, what to do, what it pays and what it opens. No plot, no twists, no endings. Almost all of it comes from the released game and stays covered until you choose to see spoilers.

blocks.text: Missions for

This chapter walks through every story mission in order, then each person who hands out side work. Each step gives who sends you, where it starts, what to do, what it pays and what it opens. No plot: twists and endings are left out. Nearly everything here comes from the released game, so the text stays covered until you choose to see spoilers.
On the map: 7 random events
On the map: 11 main missions
On the map: 7 optional tasks
On the map: 2 side missions

blocks.caption: What counts
rows: ||The 100% checklist only appears once the main story is done, under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion.||
||100 are needed. PowerPyx counts roughly 200 to 300, and every purple marker counts, including each car delivered and each meditation.||
||A silver trophy asks for 8 strands. PowerPyx says not every contact counts, so check the trophy counter before and after a contact's last job.||
||Some optional missions close for good as chapters end. They are not needed for the checklist, but they do pay, raise the relationship or give unique items.||

blocks.title: Nothing on the checklist can be missed
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says every 100% requirement can still be done in free roam after the story. The catch is the optional story missions and extras inside missions: those can close as the story moves on, so they are flagged on each page.||

blocks.title: Keep a save at each chapter break
blocks.text: ||Missions cannot be replayed from a menu. PowerPyx marks Recalibration (Chapter 1) and Checking Out (Chapter 2) as points of no return, and advises a separate manual save before each. Pocket cash is lost at the end of Chapter 1, so put money into Family Savings first.||

blocks.title: Two names for each mission
blocks.text: ||The map label differs from the title shown once a mission starts, for example Fix Your Car for Just a Scratch. This guide gives the title first and the map label after it.||

blocks.title: Missions with no marker
blocks.text: ||Some story steps are only in the mission list, opened from the storybook icon on the map: Save for the Future, Deposit Cash Into BuckMe, Take Care of Jason, Send Money to Lorena, Encrypted Hard Drive, Raul's Next Job, Heist Planning and Pay Abe's Fee. Several of them are waits that finish on their own after a phone call.||

blocks.title: Money the story asks for
blocks.text: ||Three story steps take money: Behind on Payments asks for $900 for the motel room, Checking Out needs at least $15,000, and Pay Abe's Fee in Chapter 4 takes $75,000. Send Money to Lorena and Send More Money to Lorena each send $5,000.||
